description: Cosmic Cadets is a team of engineering students passionate about space exploration, coding, and innovation. We're building AstroQuest, an interactive junior astronaut training game. We're looking for enthusiastic teammates skilled in coding, game design, UI/UX, graphic design, and space science. Beginners with creativity and a willingness to learn are welcome. Let's explore beyond limits together!
summary:
AstroQuest is an interactive web-based space exploration and engineering simulation developed by Team Cosmic Cadets. The project allows users to experience the challenges of establishing and maintaining a sustainable human outpost on the Moon or Mars.

The simulator challenges players to manage four essential resources: life support, radiation shielding, electrical power, and food supply. Players can perform engineering actions, respond to random mission emergencies, monitor system conditions, and make decisions to keep a crew of four astronauts safe throughout a 10-day mission. It also includes different difficulty levels, a mission log, scoring system, and a final mission report.

AstroQuest demonstrates the importance of resource management, engineering decisions, and problem-solving in space exploration. By turning complex space-habitat challenges into an interactive learning experience, the project helps users understand the difficulties of sustaining human life beyond Earth and encourages interest in space science and engineering.
details:
AstroQuest is an interactive, browser-based space exploration simulator designed to demonstrate the engineering challenges of establishing a sustainable human outpost on the Moon or Mars.

The project works as a 10-day mission simulation in which players manage four essential resources: life support, radiation shielding, electrical power and food supply. Players can perform engineering operations such as repairing life-support systems, reinforcing radiation shielding, restoring solar panels and maintaining greenhouse facilities. Random emergency events, including solar particle events, equipment faults and greenhouse problems, challenge players to make decisions and manage limited resources. The simulator also provides three difficulty levels, a mission log, a scoring system and a final mission report.

We developed the project using HTML for structure, CSS for visual design and JavaScript for interactive gameplay, resource calculations, random events and mission progression. It runs directly in a web browser without requiring installation.

The creative aspect of AstroQuest is its combination of space science, engineering concepts and game-based learning. Instead of simply reading about space habitats, users actively experience resource-management decisions and their consequences.

The intended impact is to improve awareness of the challenges of long-duration human space missions, encourage interest in STEM education and introduce users to the importance of sustainable systems for future exploration beyond Earth.

The project uses simplified educational simulations and does not represent actual NASA mission data.
